title: Engagement Orchestra: Renewal Sprint Guide (Enterprise + Standard)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft playbook and slide-by-slide scaffold for running a combined QBR + Renewal Sprint cadence we’re calling the "Engagement Orchestra". Goal is to provide two parallel slide tracks (Standard accounts and Enterprise) inside a single deck bundle so CSMs can tailor flows quickly and run a 30–60 minute customer review that closes to a renewal conversation or an action sprint.

Audience:
- CSMs running renewals for 50–10k ARR customers.
- Renewal managers and AE partners preparing exec-level asks.
- Solutions/Support reps who will own technical follow-ups.

High-level structure (single-deck approach):
1) Welcome + Agenda (2 slides): quick partner wins, goal of the review, ask framing.
2) Health snapshot (2 slides): product usage + signal map (adoption, errors, latency, cost). One slide for Standard, alternate layout for Enterprise with capacity & SLA telemetry.
3) Value recap (2 slides): top 3 realized outcomes + case example. Include metric deltas (MOM, QOQ).
4) Risk & Opportunity map (3 slides): combined RAG scorecard, churn risk drivers, expansion threads. Enterprise variant adds contract terms and exec sponsorship heatmap.
5) Renewal proposition + options (2 slides): renewal packages, recommended commitment, incentives, migration paths.
6) Action sprint plan (1 slide): 30/60/90 day joint plan with owners and checkpoints.
7) Decision & next steps (1 slide): finalize date, signoff owner, escalation path.

Slide-level notes (for CSM):
- Slide 2 (Health snapshot): use single-panel product usage chart for Standard. For Enterprise, split panel: usage + infra SLOs. Call out any KV cache or batching regressions (picked up from instrumentation).
- Slide 4 (Value recap): use customer quote + one visual. Keep to one slide if Standard; Enterprise gets a 2-column proof + financial impact estimate.
- Slide 6 (Risk & Opportunity): always include a short diagnostic: "root cause hypothesis" bullet and "ask" bullet (e.g., enable dedicated capacity, increase token budget, co-dev sprint).

Renewal sprint choreography (plays):
- Play A: Standard (low-touch, 30–45m)
  - Prework: CSM sends Usage + ROI snapshot 7 days prior (templated).
  - Run: 30m review: 10m wins, 10m usage/risks, 10m ask + close to renewal commitment signature link.
  - Post: 7-day e-mail with 30-day onboarding checklist.

- Play B: Enterprise (high-touch, 60–90m)
  - Prework: Schedule scoping call, collect finance and infra owners, share deep telemetry dump, legal readiness checklist.
  - Run: 60–90m workshop: 15m exec alignment, 20m technical deep-dive, 15m commercial options, 10–20m negotiation + decision runway.
  - Post: immediate exec-level recap + renewal term summary; assign SOW/PO owner.

Stakeholder matrix (single slide in deck):
- Rows: Primary, Secondary, Technical, Procurement, Finance
- Columns: Role, Name, Interest (high/med/low), Decision influence, Current sentiment (scale -2 to +2), Next best action

Risk scoring rubric (CSM use):
- Score 0–10 across three axes: Health (0–4), Exec Sponsorship (0–3), Commercial Alignment (0–3).
- Thresholds: 0–3 = Green, 4–6 = Amber, 7–10 = Red.
- Example: Low usage (2), no executive sponsor (3), contract misalignment (2) -> total 7 => Red.

Tailored script snippets (for slide notes):
- Standard ask: "Given the 28% increase in daily active sessions and the ROI noted in section 3, we recommend renewing at the same tier with a 3% annual commitment discount. Are you comfortable with that proposal today?"
- Enterprise ask: "To ensure platform parity and predictable SLAs during your scaling period, we recommend moving to Dedicated with a 12-month commit. We can include a pilot for routing and an escape clause at month 3 for operational reasons."

Data & metrics to include (minimum set):
- DAU/MAU (product usage cadence)
- API success rate, 99th percentile latency, per-route cost
- Model output quality regressions (evaluation delta) if tracked
- Seats, monthly spend, committed vs actual usage
- Security/compliance incidents or audit findings (flagged)

Ops checklist for pack creation (CSMs):
- Pull last 90 days of usage (csv) and plot MOM change
- Attach top 3 support tickets impacting outcome
- Confirm exec sponsor and procurement contacts
- Prepare 2 renewal options (conservative, growth) with clear delta table
- Pre-fill signatures/PO template or DocuSign link

Template language (short snippets for slides):
- "Top outcomes: Reduced inference cost by XX% via batching + KV caching; improved latency for X route by Yms."
- "Recommended next step: Commit to a 12-month Dedicated plan to stabilize unit cost and enable guaranteed throughput."

Common objections & rebuttals (CSM cheat sheet):
- "We can’t commit to 12 months" -> Offer a 3-month pilot w/ defined SLOs and opt-in commit at the end; include a rollback clause.
- "Costs are too high" -> Present per-token cost after batching/quantization savings and show forecast with/without commitment.
- "Tech concerns about private deployment" -> Offer staged migration: VPC dev -> VPC prod with runbook and SRE support.

Sample timeline & milestones (post-renewal):
- Day 0: Renewal signed, kickoff + shared repo created
- Day 7: Technical discovery complete, infra checklist passed
- Day 30: Migration/pilot complete, monitoring configured
- Day 90: Full cutover and QBR checkpoint

How to use this doc (CSM notes):
- Duplicate the deck folder for each customer and pick "Standard" or "Enterprise" variant slides.
- Keep the Stakeholder Matrix updated as a living doc; sync before final pricing ask.
- Use linked artifacts for audit trail (Jira, Confluence).

Open questions / TODOs (placeholders):
- Ask growth ops to provide up-to-date per-route cost estimates for template.
- Legal to draft a standard 3-month pilot SOW clause for pilots embedded in the template.
- Product to add a short telemetry export for the DAU/MOM chart to reduce CSM prep time.

Appendix: quick copy snippets for client emails (3):
1) Pre-QBR invite (7 days out): Subject: "[Company] + Redwood: QBR + Renewal review (30m)" Body: quick bullets with attachment + ask to confirm exec attendees.
2) Post-QBR summary: Exec recap, decisions, owners and due dates, signature link.
3) Red escalation: concise incident summary + remediation plan + proposed credit/term concession.

Notes to self (informal):
- This is intentionally lightweight to maximize reuse. We should iterate with 3 CSMs across AE and Enterprise pilots in Jan 2026.
- Consider building a small script to auto-populate the Stakeholder Matrix from Salesforce contacts.

END OF DRAFT
